 For Petitioner : Mr.L.Goutham Raj
 For Respondents : Mr.P.Kumaresan, Aag
 Assisted by Mr.E.Sundaram, Ga
 Order
These writ petitions have been filed by the petitioner, seeking for the issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus, to quash the proceedings of the 2nd respondent in his proceedings vide Lr.Ref.No.274/A1/2021 dated 16.11.2021 and to consequently direct the respondents and their men from anyway taking any punitive action in respect of the petitioner's product namely, HANS Chaap Tobacco in view of the final orders dated 02.12.2016, 06.03.2017, 07.09.2017, 05.11.2020 and 04.12.2020 passed in respect of the above product by the Referral Food Laboratories situated in Pune and Mysore respectively. 
2. The petitioner is a registered unit, carrying on the business of trading of tobacco, namely HANS Chaap Tobacco, after getting all statutory approvals and by paying requisite taxes. According to the petitioners, HANS Chaap Tobacco would not come under the category of food or pan https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis masala and the respondents have no authority to interfere with the business of the petitioners. 
3. While so, the Food Safety Officer, during his official duty, seized from a retailer, the product namely, HANS Chaap Tobacco under the provisions of the FSSAI Act and sent the sample for the Food Analyst, Food Analysis Laboratory at King Institute Campus, Guindy, Chennai in terms of Section 38(1)(a)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Thereafter, the 2nd respondent served the report of the Food Analyst, dated 24.09.2021 along with proceedings of the second respondent dated 30.09.2021 on the petitioner stating that the sample found is banned food product-tobacco falling under Regulation 2.12 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011. Aggrieved by the Food Analyst Report, dated 24.09.2021 and the proceedings of the 2nd respondent dated 30.09.2021, the petitioner preferred appeal before the 2nd respondent. However, the 2nd respondent vide order dated 16.11.2021,
rejected the appeal. According to the petitioner, without affording an opportunity of hearing and contrary to the principles of natural justice, the 2nd respondent passed the impugned order. 
Challenging the same, the petitioner has come https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis forward with the present Writ Petition. 
4. When this Writ Petition is taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that admittedly, the 2 nd respondent has passed the impugned order without affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and without sending the sample for re-analysis to the Food Analyst which is per se unsustainable. He further submits that this Court, vide order dated 07.03.2024 in W.P.Nos.4457 of 2022 etc., after taking note of the fact that the impugned orders have been passed contrary to the principles of natural justice, while setting aside the impugned M/S. Murari Lal Harish Chandra Jaiswal ... vs The Commissioner Of Food Safety on 5 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102033457/
2 orders on the ground of principles of natural justice, directed for re-hearing of the appeals and to pass orders de novo in accordance with law. Therefore, the learned counsel would urge this Court to pass similar order in the present Writ Petition also. He also produced a copy of the order dated 07.03.2024 in W.P.Nos.4457 of 2022 etc. passed by this Court, which reads as under:
In these four writ petitions, the impugned orders have been passed contrary to the principles of natural justice insofar as it is only in the case of one petition (impugned order dated 20.07.2022) where the petitioner has been heard prior to passing of the order. In all other https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis cases, the impugned order has come to be passed without hearing the petitioners. 
2. In such circumstances, and since Mr.Kumaresan, learned Additional Advocate General would also fairly accede to the position that there has been no hearing of the petitioners prior to passing of the impugned orders dated 04.01.2022, 10.06.2022 and 15.12.2021 respectively, let the petitioners appear before the Designated Officer,
Tamil Nadu Food Safety & Drug Administration Department, Saidapet, Chennai- 600 015 on Friday i.e., 15.03.2024 for re-hearing of the appeal. Orders, de novo, will be passed prior to 19.04.2024 in accordance with law and the Food Safety Standards,
Act 2006 and allied Rules. 
3. Impugned orders are set aside on the short point of violation of principles of natural justice alone. 
These writ petitions stand disposed in terms of this order. No costs. Connected miscellaneous petitions are closed. 
5. The learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents submits that this Court may direct the 2nd respondent to send the samples for reanalysis and after re-analysing the said sample produced by the second respondent if it is found to be a banned product, then https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis appropriate action will be taken by the respondents in the manner known to law.
6. In view of the above, the impugned order is set aside and the Writ Petition is disposed of directing the second respondent to send the sample of HANS Chaap Tobacco for Referral Food Laboratories for the purpose of carrying out analysis of the samples within a period of two (2) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and upon receipt of the report from the laboratory, the second respondent is directed to consider the same and pass appropriate orders afresh after affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner within a period of two (2) weeks thereafter, in accordance with law. No costs.
